import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Pierce–Birkhoff conjecture

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierce%E2%80%93Birkhoff_conjecture)

The Pierce-Birkhoff conjecture asserts that any piecewise-polynomial function can be expressed
as a maximum of finite minima of finite collections of polynomials. It was first stated in 1956
by Garrett Birkhoff and Richard S. Pierce, though the modern rigorous formulation is due to
Melvin Henriksen and John R. Isbell.

The conjecture has been proved for `n = 1` and `n = 2` by Louis Mahé.
-/

namespace PierceBirkhoff

/--
A set is semi-algebraic in `ℝⁿ` if it can be described by a finite union of sets defined by
multivariate polynomial equations and inequalities.
-/
def IsSemiAlgebraic {n : ℕ} (S : Set (Fin n → ℝ)) : Prop :=
  ∃ (ι₀ ι₁ : Type) (p₀ : ι₀ → MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℝ) (p₁ : ι₁ → MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℝ),
    Finite ι₀ ∧ Finite ι₁ ∧
    S = (⋃ i, {x | MvPolynomial.eval x (p₀ i) = 0}) ∪ ⋃ i, {x | MvPolynomial.eval x (p₁ i) > 0}

/--
A set is semi-algebraic in `ℝ` if it can be described by a finite boolean combination
of polynomial equations and inequalities.
-/
def IsSemiAlgebraic₁ (S : Set ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (ι₀ ι₁ : Type) (p₀ : ι₀ → Polynomial ℝ) (p₁ : ι₁ → Polynomial ℝ), Finite ι₀ ∧ Finite ι₁ ∧
    S = (⋃ i, {x | Polynomial.eval x (p₀ i) = 0}) ∪ ⋃ i, {x | Polynomial.eval x (p₁ i) > 0}

open scoped Polynomial

/--
A function `f : ℝⁿ → ℝ` is piecewise polynomial if there exists a finite covering of `ℝⁿ` by
closed semi-algebraic sets such that the restriction of `f` to each set in the covering is
polynomial.
-/
def IsPiecewiseMvPolynomial {n : ℕ} (f : (Fin n → ℝ) → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (ι : Type) (P : ι → Set (Fin n → ℝ))
    (g : ι → MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℝ),
    Finite ι ∧
    (∀ i, IsClosed (P i)) ∧
    (∀ i, IsSemiAlgebraic (P i)) ∧
    (⋃ i, P i) = Set.univ ∧
    ∀ᵉ (i : ι) (x ∈ P i), f x = MvPolynomial.eval x (g i)

/--
A function `f : ℝ → ℝ` is piecewise polynomial if there exists a finite covering of `ℝ` by
closed semi-algebraic sets such that the restriction of `f` to each set in the covering is
polynomial.
-/
def IsPiecewisePolynomial (f : ℝ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (ι : Type) (P : ι → Set ℝ)
    (g : ι → Polynomial ℝ),
    Finite ι ∧
    (∀ (i : ι), IsClosed (P i)) ∧
    (∀ (i : ι), IsSemiAlgebraic₁ (P i)) ∧
    (⋃ (i : ι), P i) = Set.univ ∧
    ∀ᵉ (i : ι) (x ∈ P i), f x = Polynomial.eval x (g i)

/--
The Pierce-Birkhoff conjecture states that for every real piecewise-polynomial function
`f : ℝⁿ → ℝ`, there exists a finite set of polynomials `gᵢⱼ ∈ ℝ[x₁, ..., xₙ]` such that
`f = supᵢ infⱼ(gᵢⱼ)`.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 13]
theorem pierce_birkhoff_conjecture {n : ℕ} (f : (Fin n → ℝ) → ℝ)
    (hf : IsPiecewiseMvPolynomial f) :
    ∃ (ι κ : Type) (g : ι → κ → MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℝ), Finite ι ∧ Finite κ ∧
      ∀ x, f x = ⨆ i, ⨅ j, MvPolynomial.eval x (g i j) := by
  sorry

/--
The Pierce-Birkhoff conjecture holds for `n = 1`.
This was proved by Louis Mahé.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 13]
theorem pierce_birkhoff_conjecture_dim_one (f : ℝ → ℝ)
    (hf : IsPiecewisePolynomial f) :
    ∃ (ι κ : Type) (g : ι → κ → Polynomial ℝ), Finite ι ∧ Finite κ ∧
      ∀ x, f x = ⨆ i, ⨅ j, Polynomial.eval x (g i j) := by
  sorry

/--
The Pierce-Birkhoff conjecture holds for `n = 2`.
This was proved by Louis Mahé.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 13]
theorem pierce_birkhoff_conjecture_dim_two
    (f : (Fin 2 → ℝ) → ℝ) (hf : IsPiecewiseMvPolynomial f) :
    ∃ (ι κ : Type) (g : ι → κ → MvPolynomial (Fin 2) ℝ), Finite ι ∧ Finite κ ∧
      ∀ x, f x = ⨆ i, ⨅ j, MvPolynomial.eval x (g i j) := by
  sorry

end PierceBirkhoff

findings.description: Lines 39–41 allow only finite unions of individual polynomial zero loci and strict-positivity loci, not finite conjunctions of constraints. This is strictly narrower than semialgebraicity in dimension at least two. For example, the basic closed semialgebraic set S = {v : Fin 2 → ℝ | v 0 = 0 ∧ 0 ≤ v 1} fails this predicate. Any positivity locus contained in this half-ray must be empty. Each permitted zero locus meets its supporting line only finitely often, unless it contains the entire line, which would include points outside S. A finite union therefore cannot equal S. This counterexample is proved in Lean as `ray_not_IsSemiAlgebraic` in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.
findings.source_evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semi-algebraic_set defines a basic semialgebraic set as the common solutions of finitely many polynomial equations and inequalities, and a semialgebraic set as a finite union of basic sets. The primary paper cited by the conjecture article, Lucas–Madden–Schaub–Spivakovsky, §1 (https://arxiv.org/e-print/math/0601671, connex.tex lines 246–251), explicitly uses simultaneous conditions f₁(x)>0, …, fₖ(x)>0, g(x)=0.
findings.suggested_fix: Define semialgebraicity using finite unions of basic sets, where each basic set imposes a finite conjunction of polynomial equations and strict inequalities. Equivalently, use an inductive predicate for finite Boolean combinations of polynomial sign conditions.

findings.description: The requirement `∀ i, IsSemiAlgebraic (P i)` inherits the preceding restriction and genuinely excludes ordinary piecewise-polynomial functions; choosing a different cover does not repair it. In particular, f(v)=|v 0|+|v 1| is polynomial on the four closed quadrants, but `¬ IsPiecewiseMvPolynomial f` is proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean as `absSum_not_IsPiecewiseMvPolynomial`. The scratch file also proves that the two summands individually satisfy the predicate. Thus this purported piecewise-polynomial class is not even closed under addition.
findings.source_evidence: Lucas–Madden–Schaub–Spivakovsky, §1, Definition 1.1 (https://arxiv.org/e-print/math/0601671, connex.tex lines 130–138), defines piecewise polynomial using a finite cover by closed semialgebraic sets and explicitly states that these functions form a ring PW(A). The four-quadrant cover of |x|+|y| satisfies that definition.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the corrected semialgebraic predicate in the covering condition. The remaining finite-cover, closedness, and polynomial-agreement conditions already match Definition 1.1.

findings.description: The hypothesis `hf : IsPiecewiseMvPolynomial f` restricts the conjecture to the incorrectly narrow function class described above, rather than all source-defined piecewise-polynomial functions. For example, at n=2 the standard piecewise-polynomial function |x|+|y| cannot satisfy this hypothesis. This is an inherited definition defect, not a separate error in the supremum/infimum conclusion.
findings.source_evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierce%E2%80%93Birkhoff_conjecture states the representation for every real piecewise-polynomial function. The primary paper's Conjecture 1 quantifies over every f in PW(A), with PW(A) defined immediately beforehand by arbitrary closed semialgebraic covers (https://arxiv.org/e-print/math/0601671, §1, connex.tex lines 130–151).
findings.suggested_fix: Correct `IsSemiAlgebraic`, and consequently `IsPiecewiseMvPolynomial`, so that the hypothesis ranges over the intended PW(A). The theorem's remaining quantifiers and conclusion can be retained.

findings.description: The two-dimensional theorem likewise assumes the defective `IsPiecewiseMvPolynomial` predicate, so it states only a restricted subcase of the cited result. Ordinary two-dimensional piecewise-polynomial functions such as |x|+|y| are excluded from its hypothesis. This is the same inherited semialgebraic-definition defect.
findings.source_evidence: The cited Wikipedia article records that the conjecture holds for n=2, using its stated quantification over all real piecewise-polynomial functions: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierce%E2%80%93Birkhoff_conjecture. The primary paper confirms Mahé's n=2 result and supplies the closed-semialgebraic-cover definition (https://arxiv.org/e-print/math/0601671, §1, connex.tex lines 120–138).
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the semialgebraic definition used by `IsPiecewiseMvPolynomial`. No independent change to this theorem's conclusion or solved status is needed.

reformulations.difference: The one-variable definition also uses only finite unions of individual equation and positivity loci, rather than arbitrary finite Boolean combinations. Unlike the multivariable definition, this is equivalent to the intended notion over ℝ.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Collect the finitely many real roots of the nonzero polynomials in a Boolean description. All sign conditions are constant on each complementary interval, so the set is a finite union of open intervals, open rays, and singletons. For a<b, (a,b) is the positivity locus of (X-a)(b-X); rays are positivity loci of linear polynomials; {a} is the zero locus of X-a. Empty sets and the whole line are also admitted. Conversely, each atom and every finite union of atoms is semialgebraic. The scratch file verifies interval, singleton, empty, and universal-set constructions, but not the full equivalence.

reformulations.difference: The conclusion permits empty finite index types for the real-valued indexed supremum and infimum, whereas ordinary finite maxima and minima use nonempty families.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: If either index type is empty, Mathlib's real sup/inf conventions force the represented function to be identically zero. That function already has a representation using two singleton index types and the zero polynomial. Thus imposing `Nonempty ι ∧ Nonempty κ` does not change the existential conclusion. This exact equivalence is proved as `mv_conclusion_nonempty_iff` in the scratch file. For nonempty finite types, the real suprema and infima are genuine maxima and minima.

reformulations.difference: The conclusion allows empty max/min index types.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Empty index types can represent only the zero function, already representable by singleton families containing the zero univariate polynomial. The exact equivalence with the nonempty-index conclusion is proved as `scalar_conclusion_nonempty_iff` in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

reformulations.difference: The conclusion allows empty max/min index types.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The proved `mv_conclusion_nonempty_iff` specializes to n=2. Empty families only add a zero-function representation that can be replaced by singleton zero-polynomial families, so this permission does not change the conclusion.

review.notes: The four findings are manifestations of one root cause: the multivariable semialgebraic definition omits finite conjunctions. All seven declarations were checked. The scalar piecewise-polynomial definition and one-dimensional theorem have no identified defect. Finite closed covers already imply continuity; this was proved for both piecewise predicates. Boundary checks covered empty/universal sets, constant functions, and n=0, whose function domain is a singleton and whose conclusion is valid. There are no answer(...) or formal_proof declarations. The source still records the general conjecture as open and dimensions one and two as solved, matching the tags. The consolidated /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles successfully; the counterexample and equivalence proofs have no sorry dependencies. No repository files were edited.

submission.summary: Changed IsSemiAlgebraic to finite unions of sets defined by finite conjunctions of polynomial equations and strict inequalities, and clarified its docstring. This corrects the dependent piecewise-polynomial definition and both affected theorems without changing unrelated declarations. Scratch proofs verify the half-ray, |x|+|y|, closure under addition, and boundary cases. The required compile command succeeds with only the three existing 'declaration uses sorry' warnings.
